neighbours.label: the generic subject of a comparison clause that appeals to how a class typically behaves ('as all bubbles do', 'the way a parent might', 'as often happens', 'sober as a judge'), as opposed to the same scene told as a single event
fire: The rumor faded, as all rumors do, and the town moved on.
He guarded the garden the way a soldier might guard a fort.
The match went to extra time, as so often happens in finals.
The old dog was as stubborn as a mule about his walks.
The fashion passed, as all fashions eventually do, within a year.
She checked the figures the way an accountant would check a ledger.
The party ran late, as these things always do on holidays.
He stood there as quiet as a mouse while they argued.
quiet: The rumor faded within a week, and the town moved on.
He guarded the garden carefully through the night.
The match went to extra time in the final on Sunday.
The old dog refused to go on his walks this week.
The fashion passed within a year, and shops cleared their racks.
She checked the figures twice before the meeting.
The party ran late on the holiday, and we left at two.
He stood there silently while they argued.
